fixes.explanation: No road back to Egypt shows up in this verse. Asaph says they did not remember His power, the day He redeemed them from the adversary. That's what he says they forgot. A road isn't on his list.

Right, it's false. The verse says He turned their rivers to blood, "…and from their streams they could not drink." The very streams they counted on were off the table for drinking. If my water did that, I'd close the bakery for the day and sit down.

Ships and harbors never come up in these verses. The hail struck their vines and their cattle, and the sleet hit their sycamore-figs. Asaph names vines, sycamore-figs, cattle and livestock here. Not one boat makes the list.
It's true, friend. Asaph says, "They turned back and were faithless like their fathers…" The psalm already spoke of fathers who were stubborn and rebellious (Psalm 78:8). So this statement is true.

No riches in this verse, baker. Asaph says Israel enraged God with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols. Jealousy is the word he ties to the idols, so that's the blank to fill. Riches would be a fun guess, but they aren't in the line.

That's the one. Asaph says, "He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men." A tabernacle is a tent, and he says God had pitched it among men. It's a heavy line, so I'll let it sit.

Peace isn't the word, baker. The verse says He beat back His foes and put them to everlasting shame. Peace sounds nice after all those heavy verses, but Asaph picked a different word. Shame is the one that goes with everlasting here.

It's the opposite, baker. Asaph says, "He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever." He compares it to the heights and to the earth God established forever. He never says tent in this verse.

False is right. Asaph says, "He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever." My cookie planet is just big enough for a bakery, so a comparison to the whole earth impresses me. He picks the heights and the earth, not a tent.

That's it. Asaph says, "…from tending the ewes He brought him to be shepherd of His people Jacob, of Israel His inheritance." David went from tending the ewes to shepherding God's people. The word shepherd stays, and the ones he looks after change.

Not a heavy hand, friend. Asaph says David shepherded them with integrity of heart. He also says David guided them "…with skillful hands." A heavy hand would be a very different picture from the one in the verse.
